title: ApoE4 disrupts interaction of sortilin with fatty acid-binding protein 7 essential to promote lipid signaling
authors: Antonino Asaro; Rishabhdev Sinha; Magda Bakun; Oleksandra Kalnytska; Anne-Sophie Carlo-Spiewok; Tymon Rubel; Annemieke Rozeboom; Michal Dadlez; Bozena Kaminska; Eleonora Aronica; Anna R. Malik; Thomas E. Willnow
one_liner_zh: 该文研究ApoE4破坏sortilin与FABP7互作影响脂质信号，属蛋白-蛋白互作与脂质代谢，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sortilin is a receptor for neuronal uptake of apolipoprotein E. Sortilin-dependent uptake of lipidated apoE promotes conversion of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) into neuromodulators that induce anti-inflammatory gene expression in the brain. This neuroprotective pathway works with apoE3 but is lost with apoE4, the main risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Here, we elucidated steps in cellular handling of lipids through sortilin, and why they are disrupted by apoE4. Combining unbiased proteome screens with analyses in mouse models, we uncover interaction of sortilin with fatty acid-binding protein (FABP) 7, the intracellular carrier for PUFA in the brain. In the presence of apoE3, sortilin promotes functional expression of FABP7 and its ability to elicit lipid-dependent gene transcription. By contrast, apoE4 binding blocks sortilin sorting, causing catabolism of FABP7 and impairing lipid signaling. Reduced FABP7 levels in the brain of AD patients expressing apoE4 substantiate the relevance of these interactions for neuronal lipid homeostasis. Taken together, we document interaction of sortilin with mediators of extracellular and intracellular lipid transport that provides a mechanistic explanation for loss of a neuroprotective lipid metabolism in AD. SUMMARY STATEMENT Lipids are central to brain health and defects in brain lipid homeostasis are causal to neurodegenerative processes in Alzheimer’s disease. Here, we uncovered how the neuronal lipoprotein receptor sortilin interacts with apoE and FABP7, the carriers for extra- and intracellular transport of lipids in the brain, respectively. We show that this interaction enables lipids to control gene transcription via nuclear receptors; and why this presumed neuroprotective lipid action is disturbed in humans who carry the ε4 variant of apoE, the most important risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer’s disease.
abstract_zh: Sortilin是神经元摄取载脂蛋白E的受体。Sortilin依赖的脂化apoE摄取促进多不饱和脂肪酸（PUFA）转化为神经调节因子，这些因子在大脑中诱导抗炎基因表达。这一神经保护通路在apoE3存在时发挥作用，但在apoE4（阿尔茨海默病（AD）的主要风险因子）存在时丧失。在此，我们阐明了sortilin介导细胞脂质处理的步骤，以及这些步骤为何被apoE4破坏。通过将无偏蛋白质组筛选与小鼠模型分析相结合，我们发现了sortilin与脂肪酸结合蛋白（FABP）7（大脑中PUFA的细胞内载体）的相互作用。在apoE3存在时，sortilin促进FABP7的功能性表达及其引发脂质依赖性基因转录的能力。相反，apoE4结合阻断sortilin的分选功能，导致FABP7的分解代谢并损害脂质信号传导。表达apoE4的AD患者大脑中FABP7水平降低，证实了这些相互作用对神经元脂质稳态的相关性。综上所述，我们记录了sortilin与细胞外和细胞内脂质转运介质的相互作用，这为AD中神经保护性脂质代谢丧失提供了机制性解释。摘要声明 脂质对大脑健康至关重要，大脑脂质稳态缺陷是阿尔茨海默病神经退行性过程的因果因素。在此，我们揭示了神经元脂蛋白受体sortilin如何与apoE和FABP7（分别作为大脑中细胞外和细胞内脂质转运的载体）相互作用。我们表明，这种相互作用使脂质能够通过核受体控制基因转录；并解释了为何这种推测的神经保护性脂质作用在携带apoE ε4变体（散发性阿尔茨海默病最重要的风险因子）的人类中受到干扰。
